complexity.notes: The validity check is O(k^2) per line (line.count inside a loop over k elements), which is fine for fixed k=9 but would scale poorly if generalized; a set-based check would be O(k). Using 'valid *= isValidLine(...)' with booleans is terse but unconventional; 'valid = valid and isValidLine(...)' or all() would be more idiomatic. Note the solution checks every line fully rather than short-circuiting on the first invalid line (list.count and the loop over all lines always run), so even the average case does constant work.
complexity.summary: Extracts all 9 rows, 9 columns (via list comprehension), and 9 sub-boxes (via slicing arithmetic), then validates each line by scanning it and using list.count to detect duplicate digits. Since the board is always a fixed 9x9 grid, all work is constant time and constant space.
